idea_year_note: c.; Aristotle's physical works c. 350-322 BCE, order uncertain
claim: Bodies with more weight, alike otherwise, cover an equal distance faster, in the ratio of their weights; double the weight takes half the time.
later_result: Bodies of different weight fall with the same acceleration in vacuum; differences in air come from resistance
confirm_event: Galileo, Discorsi e dimostrazioni matematiche intorno a due nuove scienze (Leiden, 1638), Day 1 falling-body argument; Day 3 law of fall
causal_source: Galileo's Discorsi Day 1 attacks the Aristotelian rule by name (Simplicio defends it); Stevin and de Groot had dropped lead balls at Delft in 1586
instrument: inclined plane timed by water clock

claim: There is no void existing separately; a void would remove any reason for motion or rest and make speeds incommensurable, so it cannot exist.
later_result: An air-free space can be produced and sustained; air pressure, not a horror of vacuum, holds up liquid columns
confirm_event: Torricelli's mercury-tube experiment (Florence, 1643; reported in his letter to Ricci of 11 June 1644)
causal_source: Torricelli's 1644 letter to Ricci argues against the horror-vacui explanation (secondary report; letter not opened)

claim: The first body (aither) is ungenerated, indestructible, unalterable; in all recorded time no change appears in the outermost heaven or its parts.
later_result: New stars appear beyond the Moon; the heavens change
confirm_event: Tycho Brahe, De nova stella (Copenhagen, 1573): the new star of Nov. 1572 shows no measurable diurnal parallax, so lies beyond the Moon
causal_source: Tycho places the nova in the aetherial region against the Aristotelian doctrine (secondary; De nova stella not opened)

work: Empedocles, On Nature; Aristotle, On Generation and Corruption
locator: DK 31 B6 (four roots); Aristotle GC II.1-4 329a-331b; Metaph. I.3 984a8
claim: Everything is composed of four ultimate bodies (fire, air, water, earth) that mix in proportion but are not themselves compounded.
later_result: Water and air are not elements; the simple substances are a long, different list
confirm_event: Lavoisier, Traite elementaire de chimie (Paris, 1789): Table of Simple Substances (33 entries), without water, air or earth as such
causal_source: Lavoisier's preface calls the four-element notion a prejudice inherited from the Greek philosophers (Kerr tr., Gutenberg 30775)

work: no surviving text; reported by Aristotle
idea_year_note: floruit dated by the eclipse of 585 BCE; claim known only via Aristotle c. 340 BCE
claim: Water is the principle of all things, so the earth rests on water; Aristotle guesses ('perhaps') the reason was that nourishment and seeds are moist.
later_result: Water is a compound of hydrogen and oxygen, not the source of everything
confirm_event: Cavendish, 'Experiments on Air', Phil. Trans. 74 (1784) 119-153: water formed by burning inflammable air with dephlogisticated air

idea_year_note: c.; Timaeus usually dated c. 360 BCE
claim: Fire, air, water, earth are particles shaped as pyramid, octahedron, icosahedron, cube, built from two triangles; the first three interconvert, earth cannot.
later_result: The four are not elements; matter is made of chemical elements whose atoms are not polyhedra
confirm_event: Lavoisier, Traite elementaire de chimie (Paris, 1789): water and air are not simple substances

claim: Vision occurs when pure fire streaming from the eyes meets daylight, forming one body that carries motions from the object back to the soul.
later_result: Vision is intromission: light from objects enters the eye
confirm_event: Ibn al-Haytham, Kitab al-Manazir (Book of Optics), Cairo, c. 1011-1021 (some date it c. 1027)
causal_source: Ibn al-Haytham argues against the mathematicians' visual-ray theory (Euclid, Ptolemy); a line to Plato's Timaeus was not found

claim: Some animals arise spontaneously, not from kindred stock: many insects from putrefying earth or plant matter, others inside animals from their secretions.
later_result: Insects come only from eggs laid by insects
confirm_event: Redi, Esperienze intorno alla generazione degl'insetti (Florence, 1668): no maggots in meat kept from flies by gauze
causal_source: Redi's Esperienze argues against the ancient doctrine (secondary; text not opened)

claim: The heaven as a whole neither came into being nor can be destroyed; it is one and eternal, with no beginning or end of its duration.
later_result: The observable universe evolved from a hot dense state about 13.8 billion years ago
confirm_event: Penzias and Wilson, ApJ 142 (1965) 419-421: excess 3.5 K microwave background, read by Dicke et al. (same issue) as relic radiation

idea_year_note: c.; floruit from Plato, Parmenides 127b (dramatic date)
claim: Motion is impossible: a mover must first reach the half-way point, and so on without end; Achilles can never overtake the slower runner.
later_result: A convergent infinite series has a finite sum, defined as the limit of partial sums
confirm_event: Cauchy, Cours d'analyse (Paris, 1821): definition of limit and of convergent series
same_passage_wrong: conclusion that motion is impossible; a reductio defending Parmenides, not a theory of motion

locator: DK 22 B90 (Burnet fr. 22; Plutarch, De E 388E); cf. B30, B31
claim: All things are an exchange for fire and fire for all things, as goods for gold and gold for goods.
later_result: Energy is conserved through transformation among mechanical, thermal, chemical and electrical forms
confirm_event: Helmholtz, Uber die Erhaltung der Kraft (Berlin, 1847)
same_passage_wrong: fire as the basic stuff; fire is a substance, not a conserved abstract quantity; the measure is never quantified

claim: Atoms falling straight through the void swerve slightly at undetermined times and places; otherwise no collisions, no world, and no free will.
later_result: Individual quantum events are irreducibly probabilistic; the wave function gives probabilities
confirm_event: Born, 'Zur Quantenmechanik der Stossvorgange', Z. Phys. 37 (1926) 863-867
same_passage_wrong: universal downward fall in infinite space; a single minimal lawless swerve; motive is free will, not prediction

work: lost book; via Censorinus, Plutarch, Ps.-Plutarch
locator: DK 12 A30 (Censorinus, De die natali 4.7; Plutarch, Quaest. conv. 8.8.4 730E); DK 12 A10
claim: From heated water and earth arose fish or fish-like creatures; humans formed inside them, stayed until puberty, then emerged able to feed themselves.
later_result: Humans descend, over many generations, from aquatic vertebrate ancestors
confirm_event: Darwin, On the Origin of Species (London, 24 Nov 1859)
same_passage_wrong: animals generated from heated water and earth; one-off birth, no descent, variation or inheritance

claim: Separate limbs joined at random into monsters; in Aristotle's report, forms fitting by chance survived, the others perished and still perish.
later_result: Natural selection acting on heritable variation in populations over long times
confirm_event: Darwin, On the Origin of Species (London, 24 Nov 1859)
causal_source: Darwin added a footnote citing Aristotle Physics II.8 ('shadowed forth') in the 4th ed. (1866), after the theory; no influence. Swallow, Aristotelica (2023)
same_passage_wrong: Love-Strife cosmic cycle; limbs sprout from earth; one-off hybrids, no inheritance; Aristotle reports the view to reject it

locator: Conf. XI.13.15-14.17 (also City of God XI.6)
claim: God made time itself; there was no time before heaven and earth, so asking what God did 'then' is empty, since there was no then.
later_result: In classical general relativity a universe like ours has a past singularity: time has a past boundary
confirm_event: Hawking and Penrose, 'The singularities of gravitational collapse and cosmology', Proc. R. Soc. Lond. A 314 (1970) 529-548
same_passage_wrong: a creator God outside time; time as a distension of the mind (XI.26); no physical content
